title: Compress Several PDFs While Keeping Each Document Separate
description: Batch compress several PDFs on iPhone while keeping separate documents. Check every output, page count, file size and readable detail before sending.
direct: Use batch compression when several PDFs must stay separate. Merging creates one document; batch compression is the appropriate workflow when each original needs its own smaller delivery copy.
figureAlt: Three documents remain in separate folders, illustrating batch processing without merging their contents.

cards.decision.heading: Make the first check
cards.decision.body: Start with a small representative group, especially if some files contain scans and others contain mostly text. Similar filenames do not mean the documents will shrink by the same amount.
sections.detail-0-0.heading: Review files individually
sections.detail-0-0.body: One unreadable document should not be hidden by a successful result elsewhere in the group. If a particular output is missing or unsuitable, keep that original and handle it separately. Do not repeatedly compress the whole group merely because one file remains too large.
sections.detail-1-0.heading: Set practical expectations
sections.detail-1-0.body: Space Sheep Studio develops this iPhone PDF toolkit. Its current listing includes batch compression, saving and sharing. One export-tool use is free; later exports require Pro.
sections.detail-1-1.heading: Limits and final checks
sections.detail-1-1.body: It does not establish a maximum batch size or a fixed reduction percentage here. Adobe’s PDF guidance also treats reduced-size output as a new copy, so retain your sources while checking quality. Before sending, confirm the recipient accepts several files and verify the exact attachments.
sections.detail-1-2.heading: Limits and final checks
sections.detail-1-2.body: A ZIP may help package them, but it does not replace the document-level checks or prove that each PDF meets a size limit.

steps.step-1.text: Keep the originals together in a source folder. Note how many PDFs you selected and identify any signed or certified files that need a different approved workflow.
steps.step-2.text: Use batch compression in PDF Compressor: Sign & Merge, then save the output copies. Choose the batch tool rather than Merge when separate files are required.
steps.step-3.text: Check that every expected document has an output. Compare page counts and sizes for each pair, then inspect small text, images and the first and last page.
